t:
(a) Pilot Program.—Beginning not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in collaboration with the Defense and Veterans Brain Injury Center of the Department of Defense, shall carry out a five-year pilot program to assess the effectiveness of providing assisted living services to eligible veterans to enhance the rehabilitation, quality of life, and community integration of such veterans. 
    (b) Program Locations.—
        (1) In general.—The pilot program shall be carried out at locations selected by the Secretary for purposes of the pilot program. Of the locations so selected—
            (A) at least one location shall be in each health care region of the Veterans Health Administration of the Department of Veterans Affairs that contains a polytrauma center of the Department of Veterans Affairs; and 
            (B) any location other than a location described in subparagraph (A) shall be in an area that contains a high concentration of veterans with traumatic brain injuries, as determined by the Secretary.  
        (2) Special consideration for veterans in rural areas.—The Secretary shall give special consideration to providing veterans in rural areas with an opportunity to participate in the pilot program.  
    (c) Provision of Assisted Living Services.—
        (1) Agreements.—In carrying out the pilot program, the Secretary may enter into agreements for the provision of 
assisted living services on behalf of eligible veterans with a provider participating under a State plan or waiver under title XIX of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396 et seq.). 
        (2) Standards.—The Secretary may not place, transfer, or admit a veteran to any facility for assisted living services under the pilot program unless the Secretary determines that the facility meets such standards as the Secretary may prescribe for purposes of the pilot program. Such standards shall, to the extent practicable, be consistent with the standards of Federal, State, and local agencies charged with the responsibility of licensing or otherwise regulating or inspecting such facilities.  
    (d) Continuation of Case Management and Rehabilitation Services.—In carrying out the pilot program, the Secretary shall—
        (1) continue to provide each veteran who is receiving assisted living services under the pilot program with rehabilitative services; and 
        (2) designate employees of the Veterans Health Administration of the Department of Veterans Affairs to furnish case management services for veterans participating in the pilot program.  
    (e) Report.—
        (1) In general.—Not later than 60 days after the completion of the pilot program, the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and House of Representatives a report on the pilot program. 
        (2) Contents.—The report required by paragraph (1) shall include the following:
            (A) A description of the pilot program. 
            (B) An assessment of the utility of the activities under the pilot program in enhancing the rehabilitation, quality of life, and community reintegration of veterans with traumatic brain injury. 
            (C) Such recommendations as the Secretary considers appropriate regarding the extension or expansion of the pilot program.   
    (f) Definitions.—In this section:
        (1) The term “assisted living services” means services of a facility in providing room, board, and personal care for and supervision of residents for their health, safety, and welfare. 
        (2) The term “case management services” includes the coordination and facilitation of all services furnished to a veteran by the Department of Veterans Affairs, either directly or through a contract, including assessment of needs, planning, referral (including referral for services to be furnished by the Department, either directly or through a contract, or by an entity other than the Department), monitoring, reassessment, and followup. 
        (3) The term “eligible veteran” means a veteran who—
            (A) is enrolled in the patient enrollment system of the Department of Veterans Affairs under section 1705 of title 38, United States Code; 
            (B) has received hospital care or medical services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs for a traumatic brain injury; 
            (C) is unable to manage routine activities of daily living without supervision and assistance, as determined by the Secretary; and 
            (D) could reasonably be expected to receive ongoing services after the end of the pilot program under this section under another program of the Federal Government or through other means, as determined by the Secretary.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the "collaboration", the provider agreements, the veterans "participating" in the pilot, and the report as participation. But the collaboration is with a Department of Defense entity (intra-federal), the agreements are service contracts, the veterans are benefit recipients, and the report goes to congressional committees. The Secretary's power to "prescribe" facility standards consistent with State and local agency standards does not clearly require rulemaking or any consultation with those agencies, so no outside party is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in collaboration with the Defense and Veterans Brain Injury Center of the Department of Defense, shall carry out a five-year pilot program

qwen_block.w: The section describes a pilot program carried out by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs in collaboration with another federal agency (DoD). This is intra-governmental coordination, which is not participation. While it mentions agreements with providers and veterans participating in the program, these refer to service delivery and benefit receipt, not outside parties consulting on or influencing federal decision-making. The report is submitted to Congress, which is inside the government.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in collaboration with the Defense and Veterans Brain Injury Center of the Department of Defense, shall carry out a five-year pilot program
qwen_block.b:
To determine if this section involves participation, we must analyze the actors involved in the decision-making process described.

1.  **Federal Actors:** The primary actor is the "Secretary of Veterans Affairs" (a federal official). The section also mentions the "Defense and Veterans Brain Injury Center of the Department of Defense" (another federal agency).
2.  **Collaboration:** Subsection (a) states the Secretary shall carry out the program "in collaboration with" the DoD center. This is intra-governmental coordination (federal agency with federal agency), which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
3.  **Agreements:** Subsection (c)(1) allows the Secretary to enter into agreements with providers participating under a State plan. While this involves outside entities (providers), entering into a contract or agreement to provide services is generally considered a procurement or service delivery mechanism, not "participation" in the sense of consulting with outsiders *before* making a policy decision or rule. The definition excludes "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses." Here, the government is contracting for services.
4.  **Veterans' Role:** Subsection (b)(2) mentions giving special consideration to veterans in rural areas to "participate in the pilot program." This refers to veterans receiving benefits/services, not participating in the *decision-making* process of the government. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits."
5.  **Reporting:** Subsection (e) requires a report to Congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so this is not participation.
6.  **Standards:** Subsection (c)(2) says standards shall be consistent with those of Federal, State, and local agencies. This is a consistency requirement, not a consultation requirement.

There is no requirement for public comment, public hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes/public *before* a decision is made. The "collaboration" is internal. The "agreements" are contracts. The "participation" by veterans is receiving benefits.

Therefore, the label is "No".

opus.w: The only collaboration required is between two federal bodies (the VA and a Department of Defense center), so it stays inside the federal government. Veterans 'participating' in the program are receiving benefits, the provider agreements are contracts, and the report goes to congressional committees. None of these brings outside parties into a federal decision. The phrase 'standards as the Secretary may prescribe' does not clearly require rulemaking or public comment.
opus.s: the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in collaboration with the Defense and Veterans Brain Injury Center of the Department of Defense, shall carry out a five-year pilot program
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Several parts of this section look like participation. The Secretary must act "in collaboration with" the Defense and Veterans Brain Injury Center. Veterans get an "opportunity to participate in the pilot program." The Secretary may sign agreements with outside providers. The standards must be consistent with State and local ones. Each of these fails the test:
   - The Brain Injury Center is part of the Department of Defense, so that collaboration stays inside the federal government.
   - Veterans "participating" means receiving a benefit, not helping make a decision.
   - Agreements with providers are contracts.
   - Matching State standards does not involve consulting anyone outside the government.
   - The report goes to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government.

   The closest call is "such standards as the Secretary may prescribe." It does not clearly authorize rulemaking the way "by regulation" does in Example 6, so I label this No, with some uncertainty.
